answers.responseText: Flow-chart: (1) walk forward to fix a home heading; (2) sweep the NE quadrant in a widening staircase (east leg, then north leg, each one cell longer), counting east and north steps in two tape blocks separated by a marker; (3) when the food cell is crossed, stop sweeping; (4) return by running the recorded counts backwards — west the east-count, then south the north-count — and halt at the start. Tape: two counter blocks plus markers, within 20 cells.

Keep the outbound step counts on the tape instead of erasing them during the return. Add an idle phase that burns 20 clock cycles in a small loop, then a "go to food" phase that replays the stored counts forwards (east then north), and let the machine alternate between the return and revisit phases forever. The tape needs no extra cells — only the two stored counters plus a phase marker.
I ran out of time here, but my guess is yes — it seems like it should be possible.
